newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crude firms with WTI, diffs steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crude firms with WTI, diffs steady.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes tracked higher prices for West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) early Thursday, but local trade dried up as buyers avoided a pricier Alaskan crude market.
Three deals early this week narrowed the discount for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude to $1.75 a barrel under WTI from $1.95.
Traders claimed short supplies caused the price increase.
A 40-cent rally in NYMEX crude and refinery strikes in France sent spot WTI higher. Prices for physical barrels firmed 25 cents from late Wednesday, to $25.20/25.30 a barrel.

Wednesday's buyer of ANS, which sold for $1.75, planned to run the grade at his Anacortes, Wash., refinery, traders said. Earlier this week, the refiner failed to win a bid for Koch Alberta crude, an alternative for ANS.
Instead a West Coast trading house won the Canadian barrels, a trader said.
Dealers said a tender of Chilean Rincon crude will close Thursday. The grade has a gravity of 36 degrees API.
Diffs for Line 63 remained unchanged at $3.20/3.00 under WTI.
Prices for Kern River heavy crude remained 10 cents under postings to even with postings, traders said. Diffs remained flat with no new deals reported Thursday.
Wilmington premiums stagnated at 55 to 65 cents over postings, with outright pirces $18.90/19.00 a barrel and no barrels sold.
